newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open little changed on Tuesday, on the heels of an uneventful performance in London overnight, traders said.
London cocoa futures were narrowly mixed in thin, rangebound trading early Tuesday. LIFFE September was unchanged at the midday break, at 1,033 stg, after ranging from 1,037 to 1,027 stg.

Monday, New York cocoa futures ended mostly firmer in light trading after a lower start. September rose $2 a tonne, to $1,577, after ranging from $1,587 to $1,556. Spot July ended $5 lower, at $1,551, while the remaining months finished up $1 to $5.
Technically, traders said September faces some resistance at $1,590, with the next level seen at $1,600. On the downside, September support was put near $1,545, followed by $1,525.

On the fundamental side, Ivorian weather and crop analysts said on Tuesday that the country moved into its short dry season in the first part of July following heavy June rains that favoured the growth of 1997/98 main crop cocoa.
"There are still heavy rains in some cocoa areas but for most the dry season (July-August) is here," said a national weather center analyst, adding that conditions were normal for the time of year.
